hook_candidates.on_screen: THU 14:00 · A reference for the AI?

beats.spoken: Thursday, 2 p.m. Your colleague wants an AI to polish a job reference. She removed the names first.

data.place: HR office of a car dealership

beats.spoken: She was careful: name gone, address gone. But Germany's data protection authorities say a person can be identified from the context. Their example: a job reference for a sales adviser at one particular car dealership.

fact.text: A person can be identifiable from the context.

beats.spoken: What do you do? A: Fine, the names are gone. B: She uses her private AI account, that's her business. C: You first check whether this may go in at all. Remember your choice.

The right answer is C. The authorities say: if you process personal data in AI applications, you need a legal basis for it. And employers should provide their own devices and accounts for work use of AI. A misses the context, B misses the work account.

card.title: Check first, then upload
card.sub: personal data needs a legal basis

beats.spoken: From this you can build a traffic light for the team. Green: public material, like text from your website. Amber: internal things like quotes, only in tools with a business account. Red: data about customers or staff, only after checking.

card.title: Green, amber, red
card.sub: a classification, not a DSK rule
